result.process_description:
This process begins with monitoring inventory levels in a warehouse or store.
When stock reaches a predefined threshold, an automated alert or manual check signals the need to reorder.
The procurement team then places an order with suppliers, considering factors like cost, delivery time, and supplier reliability.
Once the order is placed, the inventory system updates with expected delivery dates.
Upon receiving the stock, it is inspected for quality, recorded in the system, and placed on shelves or in storage.
The process ends when the inventory levels are updated after the restock is complete.

result.rule: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

args.text: The description says a process monitors a quantity and an action is needed when it reaches a predefined threshold; model the threshold decision and its branches. After receipt, the description says several actions are performed, but does not explicitly state that they happen concurrently.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers modeling threshold decisions or synchronizing post-receipt activities.

result.rule: When the description names a distinct activity or outcome and states its action or completion condition: Label the corresponding BPMN element with the described action or outcome. Do not replace it with a broader or narrower action, or add detail the description does not support.

When the description lays out activities in an order, or requires several activities to finish before a later stage or process end.: Connect the activities with sequence flows that preserve the stated order; when every required activity must finish before proceeding, synchronize their paths with a parallel gateway.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before the process continues: Model mutually exclusive paths for performing or skipping the activity, then merge the paths before the next step.
When the description states the purpose or destination of an activity: Include that stated purpose or destination in the BPMN activity label, rather than labeling only the broader action.

args.text: When the description names multiple required activities that must all be completed before a later activity or process end: Model the activities as parallel paths and join them with a parallel gateway before that point.
